1.q: Do I need a GPU to run ComfyUI locally?
1.a: A dedicated GPU is strongly recommended — more VRAM means bigger models and batches. No GPU? Run the same workflow on Comfy Cloud.

2.q: How much disk space do I need?
2.a: ComfyUI is lightweight, models are the heavy part. Plan for a dedicated drive as your library grows.

3.q: Is it really free? What's the catch?
3.a: Yes. Free and open source under GPL-3.0. No feature gates, no trials, no catch.

4.q: Why would I pay for Comfy Cloud if Desktop is free?
4.a: Your machine or ours. Cloud gives you powerful GPUs on demand, pre-loaded models, end-to-end security and infrastructure out of the box and partner models cleared for commercial use.

5.q: What's the difference between Desktop, Portable, and CLI install?
5.a: Desktop: one-click installer with auto-updates. Portable: self-contained build you can run from any folder. CLI: clone from GitHub for full developer control, for developers who want to customize the environment or contribute upstream.

6.q: Can I use my Desktop workflows in Comfy Cloud?
6.a: Yes — same file, same results. No conversion, no rework.

7.q: How do I install custom nodes and extensions?
7.a: ComfyUI Manager lets you browse, install, update, and manage 5,000+ extensions from inside the app.

8.q: My workflow is running slowly. Should I switch to Cloud?
8.a: No need to switch. Push heavy jobs to Comfy Cloud when you need more compute, keep building locally the rest of the time.

1.q: What is Comfy Cloud / ComfyUI Cloud?
1.a: Comfy Cloud is a version of ComfyUI that we officially host — no setup, no GPU required. Run your workflows instantly on high-performance cloud GPUs.

2.q: How is Cloud different from running ComfyUI locally?
2.a: Cloud runs on powerful remote GPUs and is accessible from any device. Comfy Desktop runs entirely on your computer, giving you full control and offline use.

3.q: Which version should I choose, Comfy Cloud or Comfy Desktop?
3.a:
Comfy Cloud has zero setup, is easy to share with your team, and is faster than most GPUs you can run on a desktop workstation. You can immediately run the best models and workflows from the community on Comfy Cloud.
Comfy Desktop is infinitely customizable, works offline, and you don't need to worry about queue times. However, depending on what you want to create, you might need to have a good GPU and some amount of technical knowledge to install community-created custom nodes.

4.q: Do I need a GPU or a strong computer to use Comfy Cloud?
4.a: No, you can start creating instantly from your browser, no matter what computer you use.

5.q: What machine or GPU does Comfy Cloud run on?
5.a: Comfy Cloud runs on Blackwell RTX 6000 Pros — 96GB VRAM, with a library of 900+ pre-installed models and support for many of the most-used custom nodes from the ComfyUI community. We expand node support regularly based on demand and compatibility.

6.q: Can I use my existing workflows with Comfy Cloud?
6.a: Yes, your workflows work across Desktop and Cloud. Just note that only the most popular custom nodes are supported for now, but more will be added soon.

7.q: Are all ComfyUI extensions and custom nodes supported?
7.a:
You can always check Cloud to see the list of extensions and models that we support, for free.
Most popular ones are available, and new ones are added over time.

8.q: Can I use my own models or checkpoints?
8.a:
You can always check Cloud to see the list of extensions and models that we support, for free.
Currently, we support a wide variety of preinstalled models.
For those on the Creator, Pro, or Team plans, you can bring in your own fine-tuned LoRAs from CivitAI or HuggingFace to perfect your own style.
Direct file upload for larger models is on our roadmap.

9.q: Can I run long or multiple workflows?
9.a: Each workflow has a max runtime of 30 minutes on Standard and Creator, raised to 1 hour on Pro. Jobs over the limit are cancelled automatically to keep the system fair and stable. You can queue up to 100 workflows at once, and run 1 / 3 / 5 concurrently via API on Standard / Creator / Pro. Need higher API rate limits? Contact enterprise{'@'}comfy.org.

10.q: How is my user data stored and secured in Comfy Cloud?
10.a:
By default, all your inputs, outputs, and workflows are private to your account.
For enhanced security features or enterprise-level options, please contact our team via support{'@'}comfy.org for more details.

11.q: Will ComfyUI always be free to run locally?
11.a:
Yes, absolutely. ComfyUI will always be free and open source. You can deploy it however you want, such as downloading it from GitHub, using Docker, custom setups, etc.

Comfy Cloud is an optional hosted service for those who prefer convenience, accessibility, or don't have powerful GPUs.

12.q: How much does Comfy Cloud cost?
12.a: Plans start at $20/mo with a credit-based model. For full pricing details — credits, plans, Team plan, billing, and refunds — see the Pricing FAQs.

1.a: Any MCP-compatible client. For the cloud connection, add https://cloud.comfy.org/mcp as a custom connector or remote MCP server, then sign in when prompted. For the local connection, your client launches the open-source comfy-mcp server: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and any client that supports stdio servers. Send the docs https://docs.comfy.org/agent-tools/mcp.md to your agent and it will figure out the installation for you.

2.a: For the cloud connection: https://cloud.comfy.org/mcp — add it as a custom connector or remote MCP server in any client, then sign in when prompted. The local connection has no URL: your client launches the comfy-mcp command directly and talks to it over stdio.

3.q: What's the difference between the cloud and local connections?
3.a:
The cloud connection is hosted: one URL, nothing to install, and workflows run on Comfy Cloud GPUs with our model catalog. The local connection is open source: your client launches the comfy-mcp server on your machine, and it drives your own ComfyUI — your models, your custom nodes, your GPU.
Which one to choose: new users should start with cloud — it is the simplest setup, and the more compatible choice for claude.ai, ChatGPT, and Claude Desktop. Pick local if you already run ComfyUI on your machine or work mostly in a coding agent like Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex. One caveat for Mac users: today's big open-weight models will not run at a workable speed on the Apple GPU, so run those on cloud.

4.q: Can I use both connections at once?
4.a: Yes. Most clients happily run two MCP servers side by side, and they authenticate independently: the cloud connection signs in to your Comfy account, while the local one needs no sign-in at all until you run partner models. Prototype free on your own GPU, then send the heavy batch to cloud GPUs from the same chat.

5.q: Do I need an API key?
5.a: In short, no. On the local connection, driving your own ComfyUI needs no key and no account. You only sign in when you run partner models: through comfy-cli with a browser sign-in, or with a Comfy API key. On the cloud connection, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, and OpenClaw sign in with OAuth; Cursor and Hermes need a Comfy API key for now. Just copy https://docs.comfy.org/agent-tools/mcp.md and your agent will figure out the installation for you.

6.a: On the local connection, runs on your own hardware are free, and the server is open source. Partner models are the exception: they run on partner infrastructure and spend Comfy credits from your account, so you sign in before using them. On the cloud connection, connecting and searching are free, and running a generation uses Comfy Cloud credits — you need a [subscription of any tier](https://comfy.org/cloud/pricing); a credit top-up alone isn't enough. Either way, your agent confirms with you before it spends.

7.a: The local connection is: comfy-mcp lives at https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-mcp and installs from PyPI with pip install comfy-mcp. The cloud connection is a hosted service in front of Comfy Cloud.

8.q: What can my agent do once connected?
8.a:
• Generate images, video, audio, and 3D — including all open-source workflows and partner models like Seedance, GPT-Image, Nano Banana, and Kling
• Build, edit, and run workflows; save and re-run workflows
• Run and read in large batches
• Search models, nodes, and template workflows
• Read and execute shared workflow URLs
• Upload and download assets for you

Everything is in natural language, with no nodes or node graphs if you don't want them. On the cloud connection there is nothing to download and no GPU needed; the local connection drives the ComfyUI already installed on your machine.

9.a: On the cloud connection, into your Comfy Cloud asset library, so you can reuse, remix, and share them — and open any run on the canvas to keep editing. You can also ask your agent to download the assets locally for you. On the local connection, outputs land in your ComfyUI output folder, and your agent can copy them anywhere you name.

1.q: Which agents and shells are supported?
1.a: Any coding agent that can run shell commands. comfy skills install adds bundled skills for Claude Code, Cursor, and any AGENTS.md-aware tool, and the paste-prompt setup works in Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw, Hermes, and the rest. For humans: any terminal, with tab completion via comfy --install-completion.

2.q: CLI or MCP: which should I use?
2.a: Both drive the same engine with the same account. Comfy MCP is for interactive agent work in chat: results come back in the session. The CLI is for automation: batch runs, CI, shell pipelines, and outputs saved to disk with --download or emitted as --json. Many teams run both and let the agent pick per task. Comfy MCP lives at https://comfy.org/mcp.

3.a: The CLI is free and open source. With a Comfy account you can browse templates, models, and nodes at no cost, and runs on your own hardware are free. Partner models are the exception: they run on partner infrastructure and spend Comfy credits. Cloud runs spend credits too, either added directly or through an existing [Comfy Cloud subscription](https://comfy.org/cloud/pricing).

4.q: How does cloud vs local routing work?
4.a: Every command auto-detects where to run: signed in to Comfy Cloud, commands route to cloud; otherwise they run against your local server. Override per call with --where local or --where cloud, set the COMFY_WHERE environment variable, or persist a default with comfy set-default --where cloud.

5.a: Browser OAuth is the recommended path: comfy cloud login opens a sign-in, and the CLI refreshes tokens for you. API keys are the fallback for headless and CI use where no browser exists: create one at https://platform.comfy.org/profile/api-keys, then set COMFY_API_KEY or pass --api-key per call.

6.a: --download saves generate results to the path you name. comfy download pulls a run's outputs into ./outputs/, and it reads prompt IDs straight from piped stdin, so comfy run --workflow flux.json --wait {'|'} comfy download is the whole loop. On cloud, outputs also land in your Comfy Cloud asset library.

7.a: Yes. comfy-cli lives at https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-cli and installs from PyPI with pip install comfy-cli, or from Homebrew. The ComfyUI engine it drives is open source too.

8.q: What does the beta label on comfy generate mean?
8.a: comfy generate is in beta: flag names, model aliases, and output formats may change while we iterate. The underlying partner endpoints are stable. File feedback on the comfy-cli GitHub repo.

9.q: Can I run it in CI?
9.a: Yes, that's what it's for. comfy setup --where cloud --api-key comfyui-... --non-interactive configures a runner without a browser, every command takes --json, and comfy validate --workflow catches unknown nodes and missing models before you spend compute.

10.q: What can my agent do once the CLI is installed?
10.a:
• Generate images, video, audio, and 3D through partner models like Flux, Seedance, Kling, and Ideogram
• Build, edit, validate, and run workflow graphs; save and rerun them
• Queue batches, wait on jobs, and download every output
• Search templates, models, and nodes with full schemas
• Compose multi-stage workflows from typed fragments

Run comfy skills install once, and the bundled skills teach your agent all of it.

image-to-video.title: Create a Video from an Image
image-to-video.description: Learn how to use the Image to Video workflow template in ComfyUI to generate short video clips from a single image.
image-to-video.transcript:
1. Open ComfyUI — Launch the application and you'll see the node-based workflow canvas where all your AI pipelines are built.
  2. Browse templates — Click the workflow templates button in the sidebar to browse available starting points.
  3. Select Image to Video — Find and select the "Image to Video" template from the list to load it onto your canvas.
  4. Upload your image — Click the image upload node and select the source image you want to animate.
  5. Run the workflow — Click the "Queue" button to execute the workflow and generate your video output.

workflow-templates.title: Browse Workflow Templates
workflow-templates.description: Explore ComfyUI's built-in workflow templates to quickly get started with common AI generation tasks.
workflow-templates.transcript:
1. Open the template browser — Click the templates icon in the ComfyUI sidebar to open the template library.
  2. Browse categories — Templates are organized by task: image generation, video, upscaling, and more.
  3. Preview a template — Hover over any template to see a preview of its workflow and expected output.
  4. Load and customize — Click to load a template, then modify parameters to fit your needs.

community-workflows.title: Explore and Use a Community Workflow from the Hub
community-workflows.description: Discover how to find and get started with popular community workflows for generative AI projects.
community-workflows.transcript:
1. Open the Workflow Hub — From the ComfyUI sidebar, navigate to the community Workflow Hub to browse curated and trending workflows shared by the community.
  2. Browse popular workflows — Explore featured projects sorted by popularity, recency, and category to find one that matches your goal.
  3. Preview a workflow — Click a workflow card to see example outputs, required models, and a description of what it produces.
  4. Open in ComfyUI — Use the "Get Started" action to load the selected community workflow directly onto your canvas.
  5. Run and customize — Queue the workflow to generate your first result, then tweak prompts, models, and parameters to make it your own.

dirDescription.controlnet: a ControlNet that steers image generation using structural guides like depth maps, edges, or poses
dirDescription.clip_vision: a CLIP Vision encoder that converts images into embeddings for conditioning or style transfer
dirDescription.vae: a VAE (Variational Autoencoder) that encodes and decodes latent representations
dirDescription.text_encoders: a text encoder that converts prompts into embeddings used to guide generation
dirDescription.audio_encoders: an audio encoder that converts audio into embeddings for audio-conditioned generation
dirDescription.geometry_estimation: a geometry estimation model that predicts depth, surface normals, or 3D structure from images
dirDescription.background_removal: a background removal model that separates subjects from their backgrounds with a clean matte
dirDescription.detection: a detection model that locates objects, faces, or regions in an image for downstream nodes
dirDescription.frame_interpolation: a frame interpolation model that generates in-between frames for smoother, higher-FPS video

1.q: How is this different from renting a GPU cloud myself?
1.a: A bare GPU still leaves the wiring to you: dependency conflicts, checkpoint hunting, cold-start ops. The platform resolves your nodes, models, and pinned dependencies into an immutable build and puts it behind an autoscaling endpoint.

2.q: Does my workflow need to change?
2.a: No. Export the API-format JSON of the workflow you already run and deploy it as-is.

3.a: Builder resolves them into a pinned, reproducible build. You can override any pin.

4.a: Yes. The engine is unchanged, and builds stay portable. Run them on your own GPU, your own server, or our serverless platform.

5.a: Pay for what you use, charged by the GPU second. Router usage draws per-output prices from the same credit pool.

6.q: How long are generated outputs retained?
6.a: Outputs are retained for 24 hours. Move them to your own storage.

7.a: SOC 2 is underway. Contact us for current status and security documentation.

8.q: Does it autoscale? What about cold starts?
8.a: Yes. Endpoints scale with your request volume. Set minWorkers above zero to keep warm workers and eliminate cold starts on the endpoints that need it.

9.q: Do I need a particular plan?
9.a: The platform and Builder are included with any Comfy subscription. An Enterprise plan is needed to share builds with teammates; governance over models and partner nodes is Enterprise-only.

10.q: What are the limits during beta?
10.a: During beta, the default limits are 10 concurrent workers, 10 builds, 3 deployments, and 500 GB of models per deployment. All limits can be raised on request.

why.heading: Maximum control.
why.subtitle: Your graph, your nodes, your outputs. A Comfy Cloud node hands off a single model run and hands the result straight back.

1.a: Because the curated set is still changing: nodes may gain or lose options, and a workflow may be retired. It is not a statement about reliability, runs are real and are billed the same as any other partner node.

2.q: Do I need a Comfy Cloud subscription?
2.a: No. These behave like every other partner node: an account and credits are enough. There is no plan floor.

3.a: Eight nodes at launch. Four text-to-image (Flux 2, Mage Flow, Mage Flow Turbo, Z-Image Turbo), three MiniMax H3 video nodes (text, image, and first-last frame to video), and MiniMax Music 3 for audio.

4.q: What actually runs on your side?
4.a: A curated workflow per node, pinned to an exact model version so a saved graph keeps producing the same thing. Your graph, prompts and inputs stay on your machine apart from what the node sends.

5.a: Per GPU-second in credits, shown on the node before you run. A short image generation is a few seconds; video is longer.

6.q: Can I use my own LoRAs or checkpoints?
6.a: Not yet. Each node exposes a fixed set of weights we host. Bringing your own is the obvious next step and is not in this first release.

7.a: No, and it should not. Keep running what your machine handles well. These nodes exist for the models it cannot, without asking you to leave your workflow.
